{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Ramon Edgar (Ray) Moore''' ({{birth date|1929|12|27}} {{endash}} {{death date|2015|4|1}}<ref name="obit"/>) was an [[Americans|American]] [[mathematician]], known for his pioneering work in the field of [[interval arithmetic]].

Moore received an [[Bachelor of Arts|AB]] degree in [[physics]] from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1950, and a [[PhD]] in [[mathematics]] from [[Stanford University]] in 1963. His early career included work on the earliest computers (including [[ENIAC]]). He was awarded the [[Humboldt Research Award]] for U.S. senior scientists twice, in 1975 and 1980.<ref name="obit">{{cite journal |title=Ramon E. Moore (1929–2015) |journal=Reliable Computing |year=2016 |url=https://interval.louisiana.edu/reliable-computing-journal/volume-23/reliable-computing-23-pp-002-014.pdf}}</ref>

His most well known work is his first book, ''Interval Analysis'', published in 1966. He wrote several more books and many journal articles and technical reports.<ref>Reviews of ''Interval Analysis'':
* {{cite journal|jstor=2004792 |last=Richtmeyer |first=R. D. |journal=[[Mathematics of Computation]] |title=none |volume=22 |number=101 |year=1968 |pages=219–212}}
* {{cite journal|jstor=23065173 |last=Alefeld |first=Goetz |journal=[[SIAM Review]] |title=none |volume=53 |number=2 |year=2011 |pages=380–381}}
* {{cite journal|jstor=1722775 |last=Traub |first=J. F. |journal=[[Science (journal)|Science]] |title=none |volume=158 |number=3799 |year=1967 |pages=365|doi=10.1126/science.158.3799.365 |bibcode=1967Sci...158..365M }}
* {{cite journal|jstor=2028021 |last=Hanson |first=Eldon |journal=[[SIAM Review]] |title=none |volume=9 |number=3 |year=1967 |pages=610–612}}
</ref><ref>Review of ''Introduction to Interval Analysis'':
* {{cite journal|jstor=40590421 |last=Gavrilyuk |first=I. P. |journal=[[Mathematics of Computation]] |title=none |volume=79 |number=269 |year=2010 |pages=615–616|doi=10.1090/S0025-5718-09-02327-8 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>Review of ''Methods and Applications of Interval Analysis'':
* {{cite journal|jstor=2029862 |last=Hanson |first=Eldon |journal=[[SIAM Review]] |title=none |volume=23 |number=1 |year=1981 |pages=121–123}}</ref>

== R. E. Moore Prize ==
The '''R. E. Moore Prize for Applications of Interval Analysis''' is an award in the interdisciplinary field of [[Computer-assisted proof|rigorous numerics]]. It is awarded biennially by the Computer Science Department at the [[University of Texas at El Paso]],<ref>{{cite web |title=The R. E. Moore Prize for Applications of Interval Analysis: Description and Rationale |website=Department of Computer Science, University of Texas at El Paso |url=https://www.reliable-computing.org/moorePrize.html |accessdate=May 17, 2019}}</ref> and judged by the editorial board of the journal ''Reliable Computing''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://link.springer.com/journal/11155|title=Reliable Computing - Springer|website=link.springer.com|language=en|access-date=2018-08-13}}</ref> The award was named in honor of Moore's contributions to [[interval analysis]].<ref>{{cite web |title=RE Moore Prize |language=ja |url=http://kobayashi.hub.hit-u.ac.jp/mooreprize.html |accessdate=May 17, 2019}}</ref>
